---
title: "Data catalogue"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("data/catalogue/helpers.R")
pages <- c(
  "data-contact" = "face-to-face and proximity contacts", "data-communication" = "email, messages, calls and radio",
  "data-online" = "online platforms", "data-citations" = "citations", "data-political" = "international relations and conflict",
  "data-mobility-ecology" = "mobility, ecology and epidemics", "data-sports" = "games and sports",
  "data-hyperevents" = "hyperevents", "data-covariates" = "global covariates")
page_of <- function(id) {
  for (pg in names(pages)) {
    src <- readLines(paste0(pg, ".Rmd"), warn = FALSE)
    if (any(grepl(sprintf('"%s"', id), src, fixed = TRUE))) return(pg)
  }
  NA_character_
}
licences$page <- vapply(licences$id, page_of, "")
profiled <- file.exists(file.path(cat_dir, paste0(licences$id, ".rds")))
vt <- table(licences$verdict)
```

This catalogue documents the relational event data and global covariates
collected for amorem: what each dataset is, where it comes from, what its
licence allows, and a profile of its structure. It covers
`r nrow(licences)` datasets.

## What the licences allow

Each licence was read on the publisher's own page (Harvard Dataverse, Zenodo
and Figshare records, the providers' terms pages, or the licence file shipped
with the data) on `r unique(licences$checked)`. amorem is released under the MIT
licence, so a dataset can be bundled with it only when its terms allow
redistribution without conditions that the MIT licence cannot carry.

```{r verdicts}
lab <- c(bundle = "public domain, CC0, CC BY, MIT, Open Government Licence or explicitly unrestricted: may be bundled with attribution",
         "no-licence" = "no licence stated (only a request to cite): not redistributed",
         noncommercial = "non-commercial licence (SocioPatterns, CC BY-NC-SA): not redistributed",
         "gpl-only" = "GPL-3: compatible only with a GPL-licensed package",
         sharealike = "share-alike (CC BY-SA): compatible only with a package under the same terms",
         "per-dataset" = "licence differs between datasets of the collection")
knitr::kable(data.frame(verdict = lab[names(vt)], datasets = as.integer(vt), row.names = NULL)[order(-as.integer(vt)), ],
             row.names = FALSE)
```

`r sum(nzchar(licences$in_amorem) & licences$verdict == "bundle")` of the
datasets that may be bundled ship with amorem (see [Bundled datasets](datasets.html)).
Three datasets bundled in earlier releases (CollegeMsg, Email-EU-core and the
Social Evolution study) come from sources without a licence or under GPL-3; their
status is under review. Datasets that cannot be redistributed are documented here with code that
downloads them from their source; the figures and numbers on the topic pages
are aggregates, not the data.

## Topic pages

```{r pages, results = "asis"}
for (pg in names(pages)) {
  n <- sum(licences$page == pg, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("- [%s](%s.html): %d datasets\n", tools::toTitleCase(pages[[pg]]), pg, n))
}
```

## All datasets

```{r all}
reason <- c("sp-colocation" = "repackages the SocioPatterns sets above",
            "snap-comm-f2f-resistance" = "many small game networks rather than one log",
            "stackexchange-or-2024-04" = "7z archive, not read here",
            "pl-statutory-holidays" = "legal texts (holiday statutes)",
            "uci-academic-calendars" = "calendar web pages")
tab <- data.frame(
  dataset = ifelse(!is.na(licences$page), sprintf("[%s](%s.html)", licences$title, licences$page), licences$title),
  kind = licences$kind, licence = licences$licence,
  amorem = vapply(seq_len(nrow(licences)), function(i) amorem_status(licences[i, ]), ""),
  profile = ifelse(profiled, "yes", paste0("no: ", reason[licences$id])),
  row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(tab[order(licences$verdict, licences$title), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

## How the profiles are built

Every dataset is read from its files as downloaded by a reader in
[`data-raw/catalogue/readers.R`](https://github.com/franciscorichter/amorem/blob/main/data-raw/catalogue/readers.R)
into a table of `(sender, receiver, time)` events, of hyperevents with sender
and receiver sets, or of a time series.
[`profile.R`](https://github.com/franciscorichter/amorem/blob/main/data-raw/catalogue/profile.R)
then computes the same statistics for every dataset:

- **repetition**: the share of events whose pair occurred before, next to the share
  expected if every event picked a pair uniformly at random among all pairs of
  the actors present;
- **reciprocity** (directed data): the share of events answering an earlier event
  in the opposite direction;
- **burstiness**: \(B = (\sigma - \mu)/(\sigma + \mu)\) of the gaps between
  successive events of the same pair, 0 for a Poisson process and close to 1 when
  events of a pair come in bursts;
- **concentration**: the Gini coefficient of actor activity and the share of events
  involving the most active tenth of the actors;
- **daily cycle**, when the time stamps carry clock time;
- for directed logs, a conditional logit on the first 4,000 events with one control
  per event and three log-count statistics (sender activity, receiver popularity,
  past reciprocating events), using the case-control history of
  `endogenous_features()`.

Licences, sources and checksums are recorded in
[`licences.csv`](https://github.com/franciscorichter/amorem/blob/main/data-raw/catalogue/licences.csv)
and in the `SOURCES` and `SHA256SUMS` files of each download.
